prompt: According to the passage, what is supernatural placement in the kingdom of God a function of?

options.text: The operation of a supernatural mentality
Length of service in the church
The laying on of hands by elders
Consistency in giving

explanation: The opening sentence of the chapter, and Daniel's promotion to third ruler in the kingdom is offered as the worked example of it.

why.a: Correct. Supernatural mentality in operation is what the chapter says produces supernatural placement.
why.b: Wrong. Tenure is never treated as a qualification anywhere in the book.
why.c: Wrong. Hands are laid on Joshua in Chapter 10 to fill him with the spirit of wisdom, but that is not this claim.
why.d: Wrong. Giving belongs to the prosperity illustration in Chapter 4.

prompt: Which king saw the handwriting on the wall and called in the astrologers, Chaldeans and soothsayers?

options.text: Belshazzar
Nebuchadnezzar
Darius
Pharaoh

explanation: Belshazzar, in Daniel chapter five. Nebuchadnezzar appears in the same story but as his father, the king who had earlier made Daniel master of the magicians, and it is Nebuchadnezzar who has the forgotten dream in Daniel 2.

why.a: Correct. Belshazzar is the king of the handwriting episode.
why.b: Wrong. Nebuchadnezzar is named in the same passage as his father, and has his own dream story in Chapters 4 and 8 of this book, which is why the two get swapped.
why.c: Wrong. Darius does not appear in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Pharaoh appears with Joseph, surrendering his throne to Joseph's divine wisdom.

prompt: Who told the king about Daniel when none of his wise men could read the writing?

options.text: The queen
The chief of the eunuchs
One of the Chaldeans
The captain of the guard

explanation: 'Then the queen came in and said: There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods.' The author adds that she knew the source of this supernatural mentality and knew it was not natural.

why.a: Correct. The queen is the one who names Daniel, and the book makes a point of her discernment.
why.b: Wrong. The chief of the eunuchs belongs to Daniel chapter 1 and is not mentioned in this book.
why.c: Wrong. The Chaldeans are precisely the ones who could NOT help.
why.d: Wrong. No captain of the guard appears in this book.

prompt: According to Daniel 5:11-12 as quoted, what was found in Daniel?

options.text: An excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of hard sentences and dissolving of doubts
Wisdom, riches, honour and long life
Faith, patience and a willing heart
Prophecy, tongues and the interpretation of tongues

explanation: Six items in the quoted verse. The first of them, an excellent spirit, is picked up later: the Holy Ghost is the One called the excellent spirit that indwelled Daniel.

why.a: Correct. All six are in the quotation, and the last two, hard sentences and dissolving of doubts, are the distinctive ones.
why.b: Wrong. Riches, honour and length of days are the products of wisdom from Proverbs 3 in Chapter 5.
why.c: Wrong. Faith and patience appear in the Hebrews 6:12 citation in Chapter 9, not here.
why.d: Wrong. Spiritual gifts of that kind are not listed anywhere in this book.

prompt: How was Daniel rewarded after giving the interpretation?

options.text: Clothed with scarlet, a chain of gold about his neck, and proclaimed third ruler in the kingdom
Given half the kingdom and the king's daughter
Made master of the magicians and astrologers
Set over all the treasures of Babylon

explanation: Daniel 5:29. Three rewards: scarlet, a gold chain, and the position of third ruler. The number three is precise and is exactly the sort of detail these quizzes target.

why.a: Correct. Scarlet, gold chain, third ruler, all from the quoted verse.
why.b: Wrong. Half a kingdom is an offer made in other biblical stories, not here.
why.c: Wrong, and it is the near miss. Being made master of the magicians and astrologers happened EARLIER, under Nebuchadnezzar, and is mentioned by the queen.
why.d: Wrong. The treasures are not mentioned in this book.

prompt: How does the passage define empowerment?

options.text: A noun from the word empower, meaning to invest with power, especially legal power or official authority
The inward assurance that God is with you
The ability to perform miracles
The confidence that comes from long experience

explanation: A dictionary style definition, and the word legal matters: your citizenship in the kingdom is validated by empowerment, so this is about standing as much as ability.

why.a: Correct. Invest with power, especially legal power or official authority, is the definition given.
why.b: Wrong. Assurance is not the category; investiture with authority is.
why.c: Wrong. Miracles are among the supernatural feats empowerment ENABLES, not the definition of it.
why.d: Wrong. Experience plays no part in this definition.

prompt: Who does the passage name as the principal source of divine empowerment?

options.text: The Holy Spirit
The Word of God
The name of Jesus
The prayers of the church

explanation: 'The Holy Spirit is the principal source of divine empowerment', proved from Acts 1:8. The word principal recurs in this book: the Holy Spirit is also the principal access to the treasure of wisdom in Chapter 10.

why.a: Correct. The Holy Spirit is named as the principal source, and Acts 1:8 is quoted for it.
why.b: Wrong. The Word is where God's wisdom is packaged, per Chapter 6, but the Spirit is the source of power.
why.c: Wrong. The name of Jesus is not discussed in this connection.
why.d: Wrong. Corporate prayer is not raised anywhere in the book.

prompt: Which three realms does the passage say the Holy Spirit's empowerment impacts?

options.text: Spirit, soul (where the mind is located) and body
Mind, will and emotions
Past, present and future
Family, business and finances

explanation: The parenthesis matters: the soul is where the MIND is located, which is how the chapter connects Holy Spirit empowerment to mental excellence.

why.a: Correct. Spirit, soul and body, with the mind placed inside the soul.
why.b: Wrong. Mind, will and emotions is a common threefold division of the soul that this book does not use.
why.c: Wrong. Time is not one of the divisions.
why.d: Wrong, and it is a real trio from this book. Family, business and finances are the three areas where crises disappear in Chapter 1, not the three realms of a man.

prompt: What analogy does the passage use for the quickening of the body by the Spirit?

options.text: Changing the engine oil in a car, after which the engine comes alive afresh and the sound becomes more comely
Pruning a tree so that it bears more fruit
Winding a clock that has run down
Refuelling a lamp so that it burns brighter

explanation: The oil pun is the point: the fresher the oil, the healthier you live. Every truly anointed person is said to enjoy fresh health.

why.a: Correct. Engine oil, with the engine coming alive afresh and the sound becoming more comely and satisfactory.
why.b: Wrong. Pruning is a biblical image the book never uses.
why.c: Wrong. Clocks do not appear anywhere in the book.
why.d: Wrong. The lamp is not used, and the oil in view is engine oil, not lamp oil.

prompt: According to the passage, what did Peter accomplish in thirty minutes on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: He had started a church, with 3,000 converts
He had healed a lame man at the gate
He had answered the whole council of elders
He had written the first of his letters

explanation: Thirty minutes and 3,000 converts. Chapter 10 restates it: without opening any book, Peter blasted the whole city with an irresistible message of redemption, and 3,000 souls got saved the same hour.

why.a: Correct. Both numbers belong to this story, thirty minutes and three thousand.
why.b: Wrong. The lame man is a genuine Acts episode that this book does not use.
why.c: Wrong. Answering the council is not part of the illustration.
why.d: Wrong. Peter's letters are quoted, but only for what he said about Paul.

prompt: What detail does the passage give about the manner of Peter's delivery at Pentecost?

options.text: He had made no preparations, yet spoke with absolute precision, with names and dates mentioned with unbelievable accuracy
He read from the scroll of Joel and expounded it
He spoke in every language present without learning them
He spoke only after the other apostles had failed

explanation: The precision is the argument: an ignorant and unlearned fisherman could not have delivered that unprepared, so it must be supernatural intelligence at work.

why.a: Correct. Unprepared, yet precise, with names and dates given with unbelievable accuracy.
why.b: Wrong. Reading from a scroll would undercut the whole point, and Chapter 10 says he did it 'without opening any book'.
why.c: Wrong. The tongues of Pentecost are not what the book highlights; the substance and arrangement of his delivery are.
why.d: Wrong. No failure by others is mentioned.

prompt: What title does the passage give the Holy Ghost in connection with Daniel?

options.text: The excellent spirit that indwelled Daniel
The spirit of might that rested on Daniel
The spirit of prophecy given to Daniel
The comforter promised to Daniel

explanation: Cited to Daniel 6:3, and repeated in Chapter 10: that is why He is called the Excellent Spirit in Daniel chapter 6. He is also called the spirit of wisdom, counsel, knowledge and understanding.

why.a: Correct. Excellent spirit is the title, tied to Daniel and cited twice in the book.
why.b: Wrong. Might belongs to the Isaiah 11 list, which the book mentions only as seven-dimensional without enumerating.
why.c: Wrong. Prophecy is not the title used of the Spirit in Daniel.
why.d: Wrong. Comforter is a genuine title from John's gospel that this book does not use.

prompt: Which scripture instructs the disciples to tarry in Jerusalem until endued with power from on high?

options.text: Luke 24:49
Acts 1:8
Luke 11:13

explanation: Luke 24:49. The conclusion drawn is blunt: until you are empowered, your place is not guaranteed.

why.a: Correct. Luke 24:49 is the tarry until endued verse.
why.b: Wrong. Acts 1:8 is the companion promise quoted just before, that you shall receive power after the Holy Ghost is come upon you.
why.c: Wrong. Luke 11:13 is the Father giving the Holy Spirit to them that ask.
why.d: Wrong. John 7:37-39 is cited to identify the water of life in Isaiah 55:1 as the Holy Spirit.

topic: the Spirit at work in three men
prompt: In whom does this chapter say the Spirit of God was at work, so that they operated above the natural sphere?

options.text: Joseph, Daniel and Peter
Moses, Elijah and Elisha
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
David, Solomon and Paul

explanation: Joseph, Daniel and Peter in Chapter 3. Chapter 10 gives a longer version of the same list, adding Stephen: He was at work in Joseph, Daniel, Peter and Stephen.

why.a: Correct. These three are named here, and Stephen is added to the list in Chapter 10.
why.b: Wrong. Elijah appears in Chapter 7 on quietness and Elisha in Chapter 6 on singing, but not in this list.
why.c: Wrong. Isaac and Jacob appear as examples of inspiration in Chapter 6, but this is a different list.
why.d: Wrong. Solomon is the cautionary figure of Chapter 5, and this list is about the Spirit's work rather than about wisdom's carriers.

prompt: What does the passage say validates your citizenship in the kingdom?

options.text: Empowerment
Baptism
Church membership
Obedience to the commandments

explanation: 'It takes being empowered to be a bonafide citizen of the kingdom. Your citizenship is validated by empowerment.' Without power you do not have a place in the kingdom.

why.a: Correct. Empowerment is what validates citizenship, following 1 Corinthians 4:20 on the kingdom being in power.
why.b: Wrong. Water baptism is never discussed in this book.
why.c: Wrong. Membership of a local church is not raised.
why.d: Wrong. Obedience is a condition for eating the good of the land in Chapter 2, not the validator of citizenship.

prompt: How does the chapter describe what the Holy Spirit did for Peter, and what it offers the reader?

options.text: He distinguished Peter, the ignorant and unlearned fisherman, so he became a celebrity in his generation, and it is now your turn to leave prison for your palace
He made Peter the leader of the twelve, and offers you leadership too
He gave Peter the power to heal, and offers you the same gift
He kept Peter from denying Christ again, and offers you the same steadfastness

explanation: The prison to palace image recurs in Chapter 11: one striking insight is more than enough to release a man from the prison and plant him in the palace. It also echoes Joseph, announced in the palace while still in prison.

why.a: Correct. Peter the ignorant and unlearned fisherman becoming a celebrity, and the reader invited out of prison into a palace.
why.b: Wrong. Church leadership is not what the passage promises.
why.c: Wrong. Healing is listed among supernatural feats generally, not as Peter's distinguishing mark here.
why.d: Wrong. Peter's denial is never mentioned in this book.

prompt: According to the Isaiah 61 passage quoted, what three exchanges are promised to those that mourn in Zion?

options.text: Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness
Bread for stones, water for thirst, and rest for weariness
Wisdom for folly, strength for weakness, and riches for poverty
Light for darkness, peace for fear, and honour for shame

explanation: Three exchanges, and the result: that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.

why.a: Correct. These are the three exchanges as the verse gives them.
why.b: Wrong. None of these appear in the quoted passage.
why.c: Wrong. Wisdom and riches belong to Chapter 5's products of divine wisdom, not to this quotation.
why.d: Wrong. Plausible pairings in the same register, but not the ones printed.

prompt: Fill the blank: "The fresher the oil, the {{1}} you live."
explanation: Healthier. Longer is the trap, because the book does connect health to long life elsewhere, but this particular sentence says healthier.

prompt: The passage teaches that a believer's place in the kingdom is secure whether or not they are empowered.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. 'Without power, you don't have a place in the kingdom' and 'until you are empowered, your place is not guaranteed.' The chapter states it twice.

why.true: Wrong. It contradicts two explicit sentences in the chapter.
why.false: Correct. Empowerment is treated as the condition of placement, which is why the chapter ends urging a fresh release of the Holy Ghost.

prompt: What does the passage say the Holy Spirit's quickening of your understanding means in practice?

options.text: That you do not judge after the sight of your eyes nor after the hearing of your ears
That you always know what will happen before it happens
That you no longer need to study
That you can discern the thoughts of other people

explanation: It repeats the Isaiah 11 formula from Chapter 2: your understanding goes beyond the natural sphere, past what eyes see and ears hear.

why.a: Correct. Going past sight and hearing is the practical mark of quickened understanding in this book.
why.b: Wrong. Foresight is claimed in Chapter 10 as a benefit of wisdom, but this sentence is about not judging by the senses.
why.c: Wrong. Chapter 8 makes research one of the four ways to exercise the mind, so study is never dispensed with.
why.d: Wrong. Reading other people's thoughts is never claimed.

prompt: Which two scriptures are paired to show that the water of life offered to all who thirst is the Holy Spirit?

options.text: Isaiah 55:1 and John 7:37-39
Isaiah 12:3 and John 4:14
Isaiah 55:8 and John 14:26
Isaiah 61:1 and John 16:13

explanation: Isaiah 55:1 issues the invitation to everyone that thirsts, and John 7:37-39 identifies the One being referred to as the Holy Spirit.

why.a: Correct. These are the two verses paired for this purpose.
why.b: Wrong. Isaiah 12:3 IS quoted in the book, but in Chapter 5 for drawing water out of the well of salvation with joy. John 4:14 is not quoted at all.
why.c: Wrong. Isaiah 55:8 is God's higher ways in Chapter 6, and John 14:26 is the Spirit teaching all things in Chapter 10.
why.d: Wrong. Isaiah 61:1 is the anointing passage earlier in this chapter, and John 16:13 is in Chapter 10.
